cleanIntro: A 1911 strip out of Dan Wesson's own series manual. It opens by asking which guide rod your gun has, because the way in differs: hex head under the muzzle means the two-piece rod comes out first, no hex head means you go through the bushing. Everything after that is common.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber cleared and looked at
steps.action: Push the magazine catch on the left side of the frame and take the magazine out, then pull the slide back and confirm the chamber is empty with your eyes. Dan Wesson puts the magazine first for the reason every 1911 manual does: draw the slide first and you chamber the round you were trying to get rid of.
steps.aside: Clear the chamber by pulling the slide to the rear.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by pushing the magazine catch located on the left side of the frame.
steps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Handgun Maintenance - Disassembly, Guide Rod Removal step 1, p.8

steps.title: Eye protection on before a spring moves
steps.action: Put safety goggles on and lay the pistol on a clean, lint-free cloth with room to set parts down in order. Dan Wesson asks for eye protection for the whole procedure, not just the firing-pin step — there are two springs under compression in this strip and both of them travel toward your face if they get away.
steps.caution: Always remove the magazine and any ammunition in the firearm's chamber before disassembly.
steps.quote: Always wear safety goggles during disassembly and reassembly to protect your eyes while handling spring-loaded parts.
steps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Handgun Maintenance - Disassembly, opening caution, p.7

steps.title: Look at your guide rod first — the manual publishes two different ways in
steps.action: Before anything comes apart, look under the muzzle. If there is a hex head on the end of the guide rod, you have the two-piece outer guide rod: put a 5/32" hex wrench in it and back it out counter-clockwise, then draw the rod forward out of the gun. If there is no hex head you have the one-piece or GI rod, and you go in through the bushing instead — that is the next step. This is the manual's own branch and it is decided by the hardware in front of you, not by the model name.
steps.aside: One-piece and GI rod instead: Depress the recoil spring plug by placing the bushing wrench over the barrel bushing.
steps.quote: Insert Hex wrench into the hex head of Outer Guide Rod below the muzzle. Loosen the Guide Rod by turning counter-clockwise.
steps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Two-piece Outer Guide Rod Removal, steps 4-5, p.8
steps.warn: Contact DAN WESSON FIREARMS for further clarification or instructions should any of the parts or assemblies shown in the disassembly process of this manual appear different from those found on your DAN WESSON FIREARMS model.

steps.title: Bushing turned under control — the spring is loaded
steps.action: With the plug held down, rotate the barrel bushing clockwise until it stops, then let the plug come up slowly and lift it out with the recoil spring. Keep your thumb over it. If the spring does not want to come with the plug, take the plug alone and leave the spring for later rather than fighting it.
steps.caution: CAUTION: Recoil spring under tension, once pressure is felt under end cap, slowly move barrel wrench forward relaxing tension on end cap.
steps.aside: Allow the plug to come out slowly and remove it with the recoil spring.
steps.quote: Rotate the bushing clockwise until it stops.
steps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — One-piece and GI Guide Rod Removal, step 2, p.8

steps.title: Hammer cocked, disassembly notch lined up on the slide stop
steps.action: Cock the hammer, then draw the slide back until the disassembly notch — the second notch from the muzzle end — sits over the rear of the slide stop on the left side. Hold it exactly there. Let the slide creep off that notch and the stop will not come out; force it and you mark the frame.
steps.aside: Cock the hammer and pull the slide back.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back until the disassembly notch on the slide (the second notch from the muzzle end) aligns with the rear of the slide stop on the lefthand side of the handgun.
steps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Slide stop removal, step 1, p.9

steps.title: Slide stop pushed out from the right
steps.action: Holding that alignment, push on the part of the slide stop that sticks out on the right-hand side and draw it out to the left. Keep a firm grip on both slide and frame while you do it so nothing shifts.
steps.quote: While maintaining the slide disassembly notch alignment with the slide stop, remove the slide stop by pushing against the extended portion of the stop, located on the right-hand side of the handgun.
steps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Slide stop removal, step 2, p.9

steps.title: Slide run forward off the frame rails
steps.action: With the slide stop out and the recoil tension already released, run the slide assembly forward off the frame rails, keeping hold of it as it comes free.
steps.aside: At this time slide should be free from recoil spring tension.
steps.quote: Remove the slide assembly from the handgun frame by sliding forward off frame rails while maintaining a firm grip on the handgun.
steps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Slide Assembly Removal, step 1, p.9

steps.title: Guide rod assembly lifted out of the slide
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down and lift the guide rod assembly out, drawing it toward the rear of the slide. On a one-piece rod the barrel link has to be standing up before it will clear.
steps.aside: For 1-piece guide rod, barrel link must be in upright position.
steps.quote: Turn the slide assembly upside down, Lift the guide rod assembly from the slide assembly.
steps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Spring and Guide Rod Removal from Slide Assembly, step 1, p.9

steps.title: Bushing off, link forward, barrel out the muzzle
steps.action: Turn the barrel bushing counter-clockwise until it stops and take it off. Then, still holding the slide upside down, rotate the barrel link forward, lift the barrel to disengage its locking lugs and draw it out of the muzzle end. The link must be forward first — the barrel will not come out otherwise and forcing it damages the slide. A tight bushing may need tapping out along with the barrel.
steps.caution: The barrel cannot be removed from the slide assembly without the barrel link in the forward position
steps.quote: Gently lift the barrel to disengage locking lugs, and slide the barrel out of the muzzle end of the slide.
steps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Barrel Removal, steps 1-4, p.9

deepSteps.title: Firing pin depressed and the stop slid off
deepSteps.action: Point the slide somewhere safe first — this is a compressed spring with a steel pin in front of it. Grip the rear of the slide, press the end of the firing pin in with a 1/8" punch until it clears the hole in the firing pin stop, and keep a finger over the pin while you slide the stop down and off its rails.
deepSteps.prose: The stop is the only thing holding the firing pin and its spring in the slide. Dan Wesson's own tip is to do it in one motion by rotating the punch inside the stop's hole so the hole walks away from the pin, which keeps a hand free for the stop.
deepSteps.caution: Wear eye protection! This step requires the removal of a spring under compression.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin stop by sliding the stop off the slide rails, which retain it.
deepSteps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Firing Pin Removal, step 2, p.10

deepSteps.title: Pressure released, firing pin and spring out
deepSteps.action: Let the firing pin come up slowly under control, then lift it out. To get the spring off, turn the firing pin clockwise and pull the spring free. Wipe both dry — this channel is where oil collects and turns into the sludge that slows a firing pin down.
deepSteps.prose: Nothing here should need force. If the pin does not want to come out once the stop is off, the stop has not cleared its rails rather than the pin being stuck.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the firing pin spring from the firing pin by turning the firing pin clockwise and pulling off the spring.
deepSteps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Firing Pin Removal, step 4, p.10

deepSteps.title: Extractor out — and only after the firing pin
deepSteps.action: Dan Wesson is explicit that the firing pin and its stop come out first; the stop is what retains the extractor. On a conventional internal extractor, hold the slide underside-up with the muzzle toward you, press the front of the extractor with a 1/8" punch, push its tip toward the ejection port side and drive it rearward past the breech face, then turn the slide over and draw it out of the back. If instead there is a small pin through the slide near the port, that is the external type: drift the 5/64" retaining pin out with a pin punch and the extractor lifts out of its slot with its spring.
deepSteps.prose: Two extractor types, one manual, and the tell is visible from outside — a retaining pin means external. Getting this wrong means levering on a part that was never going to move that way.
deepSteps.aside: Firmly grasp the slide and with a 5/64” pin punch drift out the 5/64” extractor retaining pin.
deepSteps.quote: Note: Firing pin and stop must be removed prior to removal of the extractor
deepSteps.cite: Dan Wesson Firearms 1911 Series Users Manual — 1911 Series Users Manual — undated; no copyright line or revision code is printed in the 20 pages — Internal Extractor Removal / External Extractor Removal, p.10

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Run a solvent-wet patch then a brush through the bore from the chamber end
Dry-patch until the patches come out clean, then leave a light film of oil
Wipe the chamber and the feed ramp

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME & RAILS
tasks: Wipe carbon off the breech face and out from under the extractor
Clean the slide rails and the frame rails, then oil them lightly
Wipe the barrel exterior, its locking lugs and the link

cleaning.name: RECOIL PARTS & BUSHING
tasks: Wipe the recoil spring, guide rod and plug and check the spring for kinks
Wipe the inside of the barrel bushing where the barrel rides
Keep the two-piece rod's hex fitting clean so the wrench seats fully

reassembly: Barrel back into the slide from the muzzle with the link forward, then the bushing turned clockwise to lock it.
Guide rod assembly back into the slide; on a one-piece rod stand the link up first.
Slide onto the frame rails and run it back until the disassembly notch lines up with the slide stop hole.
Slide stop in from the left through the link, then seated fully.
Recoil spring and plug back under the bushing, bushing turned counter-clockwise to capture them — keep a thumb on the plug, it is under tension again.
Two-piece rod only: thread the outer guide rod back in and tighten it clockwise with the hex wrench.
Rack the slide and check the pistol functions before it goes away.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, rack the slide and check it returns fully into battery, confirm the slide stop is seated flush and locks the slide back on an empty magazine, and check the thumb safety and the grip safety both function before the pistol is handled or stored.
